name: Savona
title: Savona-Vado Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging | Cruise & Reefer Ships
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging at Savona and Vado Ligure for cruise ships, reefers, container ships and ro-ro vessels: hull, tank and scrubber piping UTM.
h1: Savona and Vado Ligure: Hull Thickness Measurement for Cruise, Container and Reefer Ships
intro: Savona and Vado Ligure sit side by side on the Ligurian riviera and work as one port: a cruise terminal in the city, a container and reefer terminal at Vado, and ro-ro and tanker berths along the coast. Ships here are mostly on fixed rotations, so gauging can be planned and repeated. Atlantis NDT sends technicians from India to the ship and arranges the readings around her call.

highlights.h: Cruise ships on a weekly pattern
highlights.p: Lines that call at the Savona cruise terminal return on a regular rhythm. Scrubber piping, sea-water lines and void spaces can be measured on one turnaround and rechecked on the next, building a trend instead of a single snapshot.

highlights.h: Reefer and container calls at Vado
highlights.p: Fruit and refrigerated cargo ships work the Vado quays, as do container ships on regional services. Holds, tank tops, hatch covers and ballast tanks can be gauged within the cargo window.
Savona and Vado are minutes apart by road. A team arriving for one ship can usually serve another in the same system, and Genoa and La Spezia lie a short journey along the coast.

port.h: The Savona-Vado port system on the western Ligurian coast
p: Savona and Vado Ligure lie a short distance apart on the Riviera di Ponente, west of Genoa, and are managed together with Genoa and other nearby ports by the Western Ligurian Sea port authority. Savona, the older port, holds the passenger quays and a mix of general cargo berths below the city and its old fortress. Vado Ligure, a little to the south-west, has the newer deep-water terminals built outward from the shoreline, with a container terminal, a refrigerated cargo terminal and ro-ro berths. Oil and bulk berths lie along the same stretch of coast.

The traffic is varied but regular. Cruise ships use Savona as a calling and turnaround port for Mediterranean itineraries, and the terminal there has long been associated with large cruise operators. Container ships on feeder and short-sea services call at Vado, usually on liner schedules. Reefers bring bananas and other fruit to the refrigerated terminal, and ro-ro ships carry vehicles and trailers across the western Mediterranean. Some tanker and bulk calls complete the picture, along with small coastal craft. The mix means that a superintendent can find a ship of almost any type here, though in short calls rather than long stays.

The coast helps and hinders. Vado's deep water allows large container ships and reefers to berth without tide restrictions, and Savona's cruise berths are close to the city and the station, which simplifies access for people and equipment. The port lies open to southerly weather, and a strong sirocco or libeccio can bring swell to the outer areas and disrupt launch operations at the anchorage. In winter the cruise programme thins out, and berths at Savona free up for technical stops and lay-by periods, which are good windows for more systematic gauging of passenger ships with scrubber installations.

facilities.h: Cruise berths, Vado terminals and anchorage for gauging
p: Gauging at Savona is mostly done alongside the cruise terminal. A cruise ship in port for a turnaround day gives the technical department time to open pump rooms, sea chests and void spaces, and the scrubber system can be inspected from the engine room to the shell outlet. When a ship returns weekly, the programme is divided into daily blocks and results are gathered into one report. In the winter, longer stays can allow a deeper programme including tanks and structural voids.

At Vado, gauging fits around cargo handling. On a reefer, the usual targets are ballast tanks, deck structure, hatch coamings and piping, with insulated holds limiting access to the shell from inside. On a container ship, the scope depends on how many hours the ship will spend alongside, and ballast tanks, hatch covers, voids and scrubber lines are the usual candidates. Ro-ro ships can be gauged on vehicle decks and ramps between loads. Ships at the anchorage off the coast are reached by launch through the agent, subject to weather. The nearest drydocks for a full survey are in Genoa, so many ships use Savona or Vado to collect data ahead of a docking there.
list: Savona cruise terminal: scrubber wash-water and overboard piping, sea-water lines and void spaces on passenger ships during turnaround days
Vado container terminal: ballast tank, hatch cover and piping gauging within the cargo window
Vado refrigerated cargo berths: deck structure, ballast tanks and piping on reefers, with agreed limits on insulated holds
Ro-ro berths: vehicle deck, ramp and ballast tank gauging between loading cycles
Offshore anchorage on the riviera coast: pre-purchase and charter condition gauging by launch
Genoa drydocks, a short journey east: where readings from Savona and Vado feed into the docking scope

context.h: Italian port state control and the Ligurian trades
p: Italy is a member of the Paris MoU, and port state control on foreign ships at Savona and Vado is carried out by the Guardia Costiera, the Italian Coast Guard, through the local Capitaneria di Porto. Passenger ships and older ro-ro tonnage are examined with care, and a recent thickness record on vehicle decks, voids and ballast spaces helps an owner show that wastage is monitored. The Mediterranean SOx emission control area has applied since 1 May 2025, which is why cruise ships with scrubbers run their systems here and why the wash-water pipework is a regular subject of gauging.

The Ligurian ports have an unusually concentrated shipping community. Cruise lines, ship managers and insurers are based in the region, and decisions about dockings and refits are often made within a short distance of the ship. EU carbon rules add to the pressure: the Emissions Trading System has included shipping since 2024, and FuelEU Maritime applies from 2025. An owner weighing a refit against a replacement benefits from an accurate record of steel condition. For ships that trade into EU ports, the Ship Recycling Regulation also requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, which sits alongside gauging in the technical file. We confirm with each owner what the readings are for, whether a surveyor's report, an owner's decision or a sale.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Savona and Vado
jobs.p: Most requests come from cruise operators and managers of container and reefer ships who need defined readings during a regular call. Because the same ships return, we often plan a programme across several visits and deliver a single combined report. Scope, spaces and permits are agreed with the superintendent before the team travels. Typical requests include:
list: Scrubber wash-water, overboard and sea-water piping gauging on a cruise ship across consecutive Savona turnarounds, with a trend of wall loss between calls.
Ballast tank and hatch cover gauging on a container ship at Vado, closing out a surveyor's note from the last annual survey.
Deck structure and ballast tank readings on a reefer at the refrigerated terminal, agreed around the limits of insulated holds.
Vehicle deck and ramp gauging on a ro-ro ship between loading cycles, ahead of a docking at Genoa.
Pre-purchase condition gauging of a multipurpose ship at the anchorage, limited to spaces the crew can make safe.

logistics: Genoa Cristoforo Colombo Airport is the closest major airport to Savona and Vado, and Nice or Milan are alternatives for longer-haul connections. Technicians from India usually connect through a European hub and complete the journey by road or rail along the coast. Italy is in the Schengen area, so Schengen visas are required, and dates are fixed once they are issued. Terminal passes and launch bookings are arranged through the ship's agent.

faqs.q: Can scrubber piping on a cruise ship be gauged during a Savona turnaround?
faqs.a: Yes. A turnaround day usually gives enough time to measure wash-water, overboard and sea-water lines, with access arranged through the engine department. For a ship that returns weekly, we split a larger programme across several visits and combine the readings into one report.

faqs.q: What can be gauged on a reefer at Vado?
faqs.a: Ballast tanks, deck structure, hatch coamings and piping are accessible during the cargo window. Insulated holds limit inside access to the shell, so we agree with the owner which areas can be reached and whether readings from outside during a docking will be needed.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Savona or Vado for a renewal survey?
faqs.a: Large dockings are normally done at yards in Genoa or elsewhere in the Mediterranean. Gauging at Savona or Vado is useful beforehand because it gives the chosen yard a steel estimate, and our technicians can travel on to the yard to complete the survey.

faqs.q: How does weather affect anchorage work off Savona?
faqs.a: A southerly blow can build swell along the riviera and stop launch boarding. We include a spare day for anchorage jobs, and where the ship is about to berth we may suggest doing the gauging alongside instead.
